audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side rows disagreed with content win[N]. Full read Talon/Talon/Talon/Talon/Skill/Skill/Skill; content and the packet levelChart both read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Talon/Talon/Malzahar.
audit.why: The content whys are grounded — early is a genuine skill fight because your silence cuts the W-Q combo, level 6 and first-item Youmuu's are Talon's map spike, and two items is where point-and-click suppression beats a single-target diver. The full layer had the shape inverted.
audit.corrected: Sides moved to match, whys rewritten in the same proposal. win[N] untouched — already correct.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave level 6 and first item to neither side and described Malzahar's Liandry's spike as decisive; the real swing is Shadow Assault plus Youmuu's making Talon a map threat.
audit.why: Shadow Assault is 100/80/60s and grants invisibility plus move speed; Assassin's Path costs 0 mana on a 0s base cooldown (terrain-gated), so his roam economy is free. Malzahar's spike is the two-item row, not the first-item row.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[5].why now name his spike; phases[6].why states why the late row is yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Talon ability was named in mechanical terms, "Iron Boundary" was invented for Malzahar's passive (real name Void Shift), and the terrain interaction was absent entirely.
audit.why: Kit authority: Noxian Diplomacy 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, 575 range, leaps at out-of-melee targets; Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at 650 with the returning blades carrying bonus damage and a slow; Blade's End stacks to 3 before the bleed; Assassin's Path is 0 mana and vaults terrain, so he can cut off a retreat from a champion with no dash.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns, trades, dos and donts rewritten around those; the Assassin's Path retreat cut now appears in breakdown.carry and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.why: Noxian Diplomacy's cooldown is the actual step-up window and was never stated.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Q 8s to 6s, Rake 9s early, Shadow Assault 100s at rank 1, and Assassin's Path's zero mana cost.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the reader to hold Flash without saying what for, in a matchup where the enemy vaults terrain for free.
audit.why: Malzahar has no dash anywhere in his kit; Assassin's Path lets Talon get behind a retreating target over a wall. Flash is the only answer.
audit.corrected: breakdown.carry now says hold Flash for his wall vault, not for his damage.

edits.before: E a caster minion and let the visions farm for you — your lane is a macro pattern, not a duel, from the first wave.
edits.after: E a caster minion and farm — Noxian Diplomacy is 8s at rank 1 and only 575 range. Even; he cannot commit yet.

edits.before: Q online: the silence is your trade answer. Use it on his engage spell, not on poke he can walk around.
edits.after: Q online and the silence answers his W-Q. Even — he needs three Blade's End stacks before the bleed hurts.

edits.before: W voidlings turn your shove permanent — the wave hits his tower while you ward, roam-shadow, or just exist safely.
edits.after: Voidlings shove and soak his Blade's End procs — even, because your silence still cuts the Q leap out of the combo.

edits.before: Lost Chapter and the machine is complete: E-hops fund themselves, the wave is always crashing, and his tower is always bleeding.
edits.after: Lost Chapter funds the E-hops, but Assassin's Path costs him nothing — even while he decides whether to roam or fight.

edits.before: Nether Grasp online — with ANY jungle presence you now have a guaranteed kill button. The lane bends around your 6.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: Shadow Assault at 100s plus the W-Q burst can kill you before Nether Grasp finishes its channel.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: visions melt waves AND health bars. Suppress-into-burn kills through most defensive answers.
edits.after: Youmuu's turns him into a lane-to-lane assassin — he takes this phase on the map, not in a straight duel.

edits.before: Late Malz is a number: one suppression on their carry equals one won teamfight. Shield up, flank smart, press R.
edits.after: Late Malz is a number: an over-committing Talon gets suppressed mid-dive with no way out. Shield up, peel yourself.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Count it out loud if you must. - Your spell shield (Iron Boundary) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Noxian Diplomacy is 8s at rank 1 and 6s at rank 5 — that leap is his gap-close, so step up while it is down. - Rake is 9s early and the returning blades carry the damage, so stand off the return line. - Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1; Assassin's Path costs him no mana at all.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Talon wins by stacking Blade's End into the W-Q burst, then vaulting walls to farm the rest of the map for kills.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Poke with E from 650 and let voidlings soak his Blade's End stacks — three stacks is what makes his auto bleed, and they never land on you.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Trading with Void Shift down — Rake's returning blades slow you, and Noxian Diplomacy leaps 575 to finish a target that cannot walk.

edits.before: Talon spends Rake early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.

edits.before: That’s Talon’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.

edits.after: Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1 and he goes invisible inside it — shoving blind with no wards is how you die to it.
